passage:
panel — 专家小组；讨论小组
Last Friday, a public library in the town of Riverton hosted a panel discussion titled “Privacy and Public Interest: Where Do We Draw the Line?” The event was part of a series of community talks on technology and society.

transparency — 透明度；公开性
Chen argued, “but the lack of transparency.” She emphasized that even well-intentioned projects can damage trust if people are not informed about how their data is used.

whistleblower — 举报人；揭发者
He argued that whistleblower protections are essential for a free press and for keeping powerful institutions in check.

consent — 同意；许可
Transparency, she noted, allows individuals to consent meaningfully and holds organizations accountable.

beneficial — 有益的；有利的
During the question-and-answer session, a student asked whether public-interest projects should be allowed to use data without consent if the project is clearly beneficial.

evaluate — 评估；评价
She suggested that an independent review board should evaluate each case.

proposed — 提议；建议
Nair proposed a middle path: “We can require companies to explain their data use in plain language.

attendee — 参加者；出席者
Now I see it affects everyone.” Another attendee, a local business owner, remarked that the discussion made him reconsider how his own company handles customer information.
